title: Recording: I Lie Around by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Alan Parsons

Wings worked on the ‘Live And Let Die’ single’s b-side ‘I Lie Around’ on 27 September 1972.

It was recorded during the during the Ram sessions in New York City in 1970, though it remained unfinished at the time.

It was originally recorded for the Ram sessions, but finished in the UK. I don’t remember if it was at Abbey Road or Olympic Studios. I sang some backing vocals. Some of the guitar licks sound like Henry McCullough, but I’m not sure and Paul played a lot of the guitar solos too.
Denny Seiwell
Paul McCartney Recording Sessions (1969-2013), Luca Perasi

Although Paul McCartney had recorded lead vocals in New York, on this day he decided to try the song out with Denny Laine singing. Between 1.30pm and 6.30pm Laine double-tracked new lead vocals. McCartney’s original vocals can be heard towards the song’s end, including in the final verse.

Page last updated: 25 November 2025
